note:
C3/C4 READOUT (crucial physics):
- C3 level ladder (constant b, single blob NO KICK): alive & static at b in [-0.15,+0.2],
  area shifts 46->25 px (b<0 = bigger blob, b>0 = smaller: same trend as vvw isod
  'toward smaller d = bigger species'). Static window comfortably wide.
- C3 pair at b=+0.1: STATIC (c=0) — tau_c(pair) grows with b (smaller blob = less drive).
- C3 pair at b=-0.1: REPLICATION cascade at t=70! At b=-0.1 the world (at tau=5.7)
  is past its replication edge for PAIRS (singles fine, static, area 36).
- C4 drift (saw, parked single at b=0):
  * The blob drifts DOWN-b (-x on rising branch): downstream=-x as expected.
  * BUT the drift velocity is HUGE near onset: -0.08 px/tu at eps=0.00125 (b_loc~-0.02),
    NOT ~0.906*eps ~ 0.001. Because tau=5.7 sits 0.048 below the SINGLE drift
    bifurcation (tau_c=5.748), the parked blob is nearly marginal: the gradient
    doesn't push a stiff blob, it UNLEASHES the drift mode down-b. v is not linear
    in eps; it's near-onset ballistic.
  * At eps=0.00125 blob runs down to trough (x~0..3), oscillates/settles there, area fine.
  * eps>=0.0025: the DOWN-B RUN destabilizes the blob: moving blob at local
    b <= ~ -0.09..-0.13 REPLICATES (b=-0.1 replication edge, consistent with C3 pair).
    The saw trough depth -eps*40.8: eps=0.0025 -> b_min=-0.102 (just past edge!).
So: the adversary is much stronger than the vvw analogue, and the LOW-b side is the
dangerous side (replication of down-running blobs at b<~-0.09).
DESIGN CONSEQUENCES:
1. Saw must be SHALLOW enough that trough b_min > ~-0.06 (safety margin from -0.09):
   with n_teeth=1, frac=0.85, b spans +-eps*40.8 -> eps <= 0.0015. OR shift/clip the
   profile asymmetrically (b_offset) to keep b in a safe band, e.g. b in [-0.05, +0.1]:
   the up side is much safer (pairs static at +0.1, singles fine to +0.2).
2. tau=5.7 lone cargo is NOT immobile on the slope (near-onset unleashing).
   'Parked cargo stays put' needs LOWER tau (deeper in pair-only zone, more sub-onset)
   or shallower local slope at park points. C2 confirmed decay-to-rest at b flat;
   on a slope the C4 e0.00125 run shows a down-b runaway to the trough.
   => cargo CAN be parked at/near the TROUGH (its natural resting place!): machine
   picks cargo up from the trough and drags it up the long branch. That's even the
   honest 'worst case' cargo position: maximum required lift.
3. v_drift(eps) for the baseline: measure at the working eps with the C4 protocol
   but report the measured curve (nonlinear near onset). At eps=0.00125 the initial
   run is v=-0.083..-0.05 while ON the slope: |v_drift| ~ 0.05 comparable to c_pair
   0.059! The pair barely outruns the single's downhill run at this tau.
   => consider tau slightly lower (5.68) to slow the adversary more than the pair?
   No — both scale together. Better: the efficiency baseline uses the MEASURED
   |v_drift| on the working track (locked metric already says C4-measured).

mechanism: RELAY TUG: loco 3-train picks up trough-parked cargoes head-on (each locks as NEW LEADER, gap 14.4-15.4): 4-train t=270, 5-train t=600, 6-train t=915. Near t~1000-1900 the 6-train FISSIONS from the rear (near-onset power limit): rear loco blobs shed one by one, regroup as a trailing 3-train; the front trio == THE THREE CARGOES continues as a self-propelled upstream train at c~0.07. note: CERT BATTERY v1 (no rails) FAILED under working noise sigma=2e-3: 3 seeds all show TRAIN BUCKLING after 1-2 pickups (t~900-1500): the train bends off-axis and reorients into the saw TROUGH VALLEY, ending as a y-circulating cluster at x~trough (zero-climb direction; the trough transversely confines it). Pickups before buckle: seed1=1, seed2=2, seed3=1; net_up 29.9/59.7/30.7 px — b6 n_cycles FAIL. Noiseless pilot had worked (y-symmetry exact). MECHANISM: near-onset train propagation direction is soft; up-slope is the hardest direction; noise nucleates a turn toward the free y-direction. THE FIX (brief candidate (a): 'rails keep the train on axis'): static y-channel added to the load field, b(x,y)=saw(x)+chan_eps*min(|y-L/2|,cap) — same static-environment class as the saw. Single-species world has no self-assembled stripe walls (M4 never built them) — rails as static field is the v1 approach, documented honestly.
